- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >5% from recent high, model underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >85 and true outcome is <75, adjust downward by 10–15% to reflect momentum correction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use 5-day rolling average of true values to anchor forecast mid-point.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag: if true outcome is 5–10% below 30d forecast, adjust downward by 1–2% for next period to account for delayed reaction.
